name: apple-notes-mcp
description: Read, search and write Apple Notes through the Notes app
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift that gives Claude access to the Notes app on this Mac.

Notes has no framework a separate process can use, so this server drives Notes.app itself through Apple events. Notes must be running, and the grant appears under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Automation.

Notes are returned as plain text by default rather than HTML: it is what you actually want to read, and it costs a fraction of the tokens.

update_note makes you say whether you are appending or replacing. Silently replacing a long note is the mistake worth designing against.

Tags and pinning are not here. Notes' scripting dictionary does not expose them at all — they need the Shortcuts server instead.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: notes_status
tools.description: Reports whether Notes is running, whether this server may automate it, and what limits are in force. Reads no notes.

tools.name: notes_accounts
tools.description: Lists every Notes account — iCloud, On My Mac, an Exchange account — with how many folders each holds.

tools.name: notes_folders
tools.description: Lists every folder with its account, its note count, and the path to address it by. Nested folders appear as 'Parent/Child'.

tools.name: notes_search
tools.description: Finds notes by text, folder, account and date range. Returns one line per note with its id — never the note's contents. Follow it with note_get.

tools.name: note_get
tools.description: Returns one note's text with its folder, dates and attachment count.

tools.name: note_attachments
tools.description: Lists what is attached to one note: name, dates, the link a URL attachment points at, and the cid: reference it appears under in the note's HTML.

tools.name: create_note
tools.description: Adds a new note to a folder. The note's title is the first line of the body, because that is how Notes works — there is no separate title.

tools.name: update_note
tools.description: Changes a note's content. 'mode' is REQUIRED and decides which of two very different things happens:

tools.name: move_note
tools.description: Moves a note into a different folder. Its content is untouched.

tools.name: delete_note
tools.description: Deletes a note. Requires confirm=true, and returns the full record it removed — including the text — so what was lost is at least written down somewhere.
